belief: “Other people had it worse, so what was done to me doesn’t really count.”
belief_plain: Other people had it worse, so what was done to me doesn’t really count
origins: Comparison is a way to keep going: “Other people had it worse, so mine doesn’t count.” Sometimes other people said that to silence you. Minimizing can feel humble or tough. It is still a lie if it means your harm does not matter, you should not need help, and you should not tell. Someone else’s deeper pain does not shrink yours. God does not run a contest before He binds up the brokenhearted. You do not have to prove your story was the worst in order for it to count. If you are not safe right now, call 911. You can also call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233. If a child is being hurt, call Childhelp at 1-800-422-4453. A counselor can help you at a pace that is safe. You do not have to do this alone, or all at once.
self: I should be over it because others had it worse.
If I get help, I am taking it from someone who needs it more.
I have no right to call it abuse.
God is busy with bigger suffering.
replacement: What was done to me counts, even if someone else suffered more. I am allowed to get help without winning a comparison.
